notes.text: The forward lines keep changing. Even their four most-used trios over the last 10 games cover only 31% of their forwards’ 5-on-5 time, the 7th-lowest in the league (a typical team: 40%). The lines listed lean on their latest games, but expect new combinations tonight.

Rasmus Ristolainen is out and has missed the last 6 games. Jamie Drysdale has taken his spot beside Travis Sanheim. That pair has had 53% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 88:13 together, up from 23% with Ristolainen.
Nikita Grebenkin is out at least four months (back surgery) and has not played this season. Sean Couturier has taken his spot beside Owen Tippett and Trevor Zegras.
David Jiříček has started playing on the power play: on the ice for 43% of the team’s power-play time in 9 games, up from 2% last season.
Colton Dach is out (illness) and has missed the last 2 games. Zach Hyman has taken his spot beside Ryan Nugent-Hopkins and Kasperi Kapanen.

Matt Savoie is on long-term injured reserve (lower-body injury) and has not played this season. Leon Draisaitl has taken his spot beside Connor McDavid and Vasily Podkolzin. That line has had 63% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 209:19 together.
Zach Hyman returned in their last game after missing 5 games. Their recent numbers were built mostly without him.
Kasperi Kapanen has started playing on the power play: on the ice for 52% of the team’s power-play time in 18 games, up from 6% last season.
Ty Emberson is no longer killing penalties: 4% of the team’s shorthanded time in 14 games, down from 30% last season.

EDM.head: The Oilers have a lot going for them
EDM.body: Edmonton has been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately and has home-ice advantage. The Flyers can make it interesting if their power play gets going.

PHI.head: The Flyers have a hill to climb
PHI.body: Edmonton has been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately and has home-ice advantage. The Flyers can pull it off if their power play gets going.

story.head: Expect a grind
paras: The Oilers (12-3-3) beat Vancouver 4-2 on Saturday, while the Flyers are winless in three (0-2-1). Going in, the Flyers are last in the Metropolitan (29th in the NHL) and the Oilers first in the Pacific (tied for third).

The Flyers haven’t played well, but their record (.342) is worse than their play: their chances are worth about .394, and their finishing has held them back. The Oilers’ record (.750) is running ahead of what their chances are worth (.595), largely thanks to their finishing.

The Flyers pick their shots (3rd lowest) and get a lot of their shots blocked (30th). Philadelphia has scored 2.21 goals a game, the second fewest in the league. As for the Oilers, they ice the puck less than almost anyone (2nd) and have a dangerous power play (2nd). They also lean hard on their top players (lowest), so the Flyers roll four lines, but them lean on their top six. Edmonton has scored 4.11 goals a game, the most in the league. Both teams play slow, low-event hockey, especially the Flyers (2nd lowest), so expect a tight one.

Trevor Zegras (4 G / 10 A / 14 P in 19 GP) leads the Flyers in scoring, and Matvei Michkov (10 G / 3 A / 13 P in 19 GP) has a team-high ten goals. Connor McDavid (10 G / 37 A / 47 P in 18 GP) leads the Oilers and the whole NHL in scoring, with eleven points in his last five games. Leon Draisaitl (16 G / 18 A / 34 P in 18 GP) has a team-high 16 goals, tied for the most in the NHL, with ten points in his last five games.

Tristan Jarry (4-1-3 / .898 SV% in 8 GS) will likely start for Edmonton. Philadelphia has two options in net: Dan Vladař (3-4-3 / .880 SV% in 10 GS) and Joseph Woll (1-6-2 / .898 SV% in 9 GS). Vladař has started six of their last ten games, including the last one on Sunday. It’s anyone’s guess who gets the net. Vladař has a .927 save percentage in six starts against the Oilers, well above his usual .894. Don’t read much into it: a goalie’s record against one team rarely holds up.
At home, Mike Babcock likes to send Jones, Michaels and Frederic out against opponents’ fourth lines, so watch for them against Barkey, Couturier and Acciari.
